children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me begin with a few questions.

**First, could you please tell me the names of all the children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex. They're 8 years old, and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To determine eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask a few more questions about your circumstances.

**Are you responsible for Alex - that is, do you live with Alex and do they live with you as part of your household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. They live with their other parent. But I do help out financially - I contribute towards their upkeep each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

**Do you have any legal responsibility for Alex, such as through a court order, formal agreement, or are you the named parent on their birth certificate?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm their parent - I'm on the birth certificate.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's useful to know.

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have a National Insurance number?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm here in England. And yes, I have a National Insurance number.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that.

**One more important question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has a claim been made for Alex by another person?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:

- You are Alex's parent (named on the birth certificate)
- You live in the UK (England)
- You have a National Insurance number
- Alex is 8 years old
- Alex does not live with you, but lives with their other parent
- You do contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Unfortunately, under UK Child Benefit rules, **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**. Here's why:

Child Benefit can only be claimed by the person who is responsible for the child, which means the child must live with you and you must be looking after them. Since Alex lives with their other parent and is being looked after by them, the person living with Alex and responsible for their day-to-day care would be the eligible claimant, not you.

While your financial contributions are commendable and may be relevant to other support you could receive, they don't establish the responsibility needed for Child Benefit eligibility.
